main_body: Wooden rack frame holding five kegs seen end-on (barrel faces with gold bands) in two tiers, with a plank top beam and a bottom beam
top_band: Rows 8-12: orange-brown plank band at the top (rows 9-12), about 4-5 rows. It is the front of the top beam, a flat face with a lighter strip at row 12, not a horizontal surface seen from above. Below it is the open front with kegs.
evidence: The whole rack is drawn straight on from the front. The top beam is a flat band with a light line at row 12 and a darker shadow under it, so it reads as the face of the beam. The kegs show only circular end faces, with no top surfaces. The bottom beam at rows 29-30 is a thin strip with no visible top. The uprights are vertical strips. No horizontal surface reads as seen from above, so the piece is a front elevation with a hat.

style.evidence: The keg ends have a few shading steps (ring, wood, gold bung, dark shadow), and the outlines are dark brown rather than black. The top beam is a mostly flat orange band with little grain. The grey background areas inside the frame are flat and checker-dithered. Compared with the stall and well references it has fewer steps and less per-tile variation, though it is not a bare flat fill.
